text:
mike: Opening this thread for a weird mobile-only repro. iOS/Android clients on flaky cellular networks sometimes see reassembled SSE streams where chunks are out of order after a handoff (wifi->cell), and we get missing separators or duplicated fragments. Repro in our mobile SDK sample app when cellular switching happens mid-stream.

anya: do you have packet captures or logs? mobile networks can reorder TCP segments at the radio layer during handoff, but SSE over HTTP/2 should still be in-order. is there a proxy or browser shim on mobile doing retries?

mike: there's a tiny proxy in front of our edge that does auth and short buffering. Captured fragments from an iOS run where network switched while the stream was open:

```
# initial stream (on wifi)
frag1: "id: 9001\nevent: delta\ndata: chunk-A-part1\n"
frag2: "data: -A-part2\n\n"
# handoff occurs, device reconnects quickly with Last-Event-ID: 9001
# proxy replay/merge behavior during handoff + gzip interaction
frag3 (resume): "id: 9001\nevent: delta\ndata: chunk-A-part2\n\nid: 9002\nevent: delta\ndata: chunk-B-full\n\n"
# but mobile client also receives a delayed packet from the old connection with remainder of frag1 after frag3
frag4 (late): "data: -A-part3\n\n"
```

mike: result on iOS: app shows A-part1 + A-part2 + A-part2 + A-part3 in that order (dup and split). Android client (Kotlin) tends to drop late packets by timing out the old socket and prevents reordering, but iOS uses CFNetwork and the reconnect code kept both streams alive briefly and merged buffers.

oliver: two interesting failure modes: 1) proxy rewrites Content-Encoding/gzip and can split compressed frames unpredictably (we saw the proxy decompress + re-chunk on resume), 2) the mobile SDK reuses a shared buffer pool and a late read from old socket can overwrite the buffer contents used by the resumed stream if we don't copy immutably. Both can produce dupes or corruption.

anya: SDK fixes I can think of: a) when resuming with Last-Event-ID, snapshot last_seen_id and drop any partial buffer state, b) serialize reconnect attempts (single inflight resume per client), c) ensure reads from any socket allocate fresh immutable buffers (no shared pooling between connections), d) normalize decompression path: if proxy may change Content-Encoding on resume, treat bodies as opaque byte streams and avoid attempting incremental gzip reassembly at the client.

mike: on iOS we were trying to be efficient and keep a reusable Data buffer across reads, which allowed the late fragment to mutate the data used by the resumed stream. Changed to copy Bytes before handing to parser fixed one class of dupes.

oliver: for mobile specifically add an extra defensive check: if an incoming frame has an id <= Last-Event-ID on resume, drop it; if it has id == Last-Event-ID but the data equals the last emitted payload suffix, skip emitting (simple dedupe by equality). This helps when servers retransmit suffixes.

anya: also watch out for compression: if proxy decompresses and then sends resumed bytes without aligning to SSE boundaries, client should treat any leading bytes that do not start with an `id:` or blank-line as potential continuation — but if we're resuming, prefer to discard continuations and wait for a fresh `id:` line. That prevents garbling when server doesn't retransmit full events.

infra: ci: mobile-sdk-stream-tests flaky (iOS handoff) in build #2026.09.12-512. https://ci.redwood.example/2026/09/12/512

mike: mitigation for quickstart: bump mobile sample's stream_timeout to 120s and set reconnect_backoff to 800ms to reduce rapid reconnects during handoffs. Also added a note in the mobile SDK README about flaky cellular handoffs and recommended config.

oliver: i'll send a small PR for SDK changes: 1) reconnect mutex, 2) copy-on-read buffer, 3) drop partials on resume + id filtering, 4) unit tests simulating delayed old-socket fragments and proxy decompress jitter.

anya: i'll add integration jobs to the mobile CI that run a wifi->cell handoff simulation (use the network emulator to pause and resume connections) and inject a late fragment after resume to ensure we don't reorder.

mike: thanks — ping me for logs. also filing customer impact ticket and will backport once tests are green. :shipit:
